title: ChatGPT Mobile Gets Major UI Redesign; Dots Expands Testing and Integrates Health Data

content_html:
ChatGPT, which has about 1.2 billion weekly active users, is getting a significant interaction update on mobile. On November 20, OpenAI began rolling out a new version of the ChatGPT mobile app interface to some users. The main goal is to help users reach frequently used features faster and lower the barrier to discovering new capabilities. This interface redesign is first available to ChatGPT Pro users who already have Dots or are eligible to create them, and it also includes a small number of eligible Plus users in the experience.

Interface redesign: Dots becomes a standalone bottom tab, and commonly used tools can be customized and pinned

For quite a long time, ChatGPT’s overall layout has remained fairly stable: the prompt input box sits in the center, while the left navigation bar serves as the entry point for switching among features such as Dots, Spaces, Images, and Codex.

The new mobile interface changes this path: Dots gets its own tab at the bottom of the home screen, so users can access it directly without having to dig through the navigation bar. At the same time, users can pin commonly used features such as Codex, Projects, and Images to the bottom tab bar based on their personal habits, further shortening the path to frequently used tools.

According to the rollout rules, the new design is available to ChatGPT Pro users who are at least 18 years old and located in regions where Dots is supported, as well as some eligible Plus users; however, it is not being rolled out in the European Economic Area (including the EU), the UK, Switzerland, or South Korea for now. Users can update the app to the latest version, and if the new interface does not appear by default, they can also enable it manually in Settings.

Dots expands testing and proactive service: gradual rollout to Plus and Business Standard

Along with the interface changes, the testing scope for Dots is also expanding further. Previously, Dots was only available to ChatGPT Pro subscribers, with plans starting at $100 per month; now, OpenAI has begun testing Dots with a small number of ChatGPT Plus users and is gradually rolling it out to ChatGPT Business Standard users.

An OpenAI executive said the team is still continuously collecting user feedback, and noted that after multiple rounds of improvements, Dots has received more positive feedback for its proactive service. Dots will also be opened up to a broader audience in the future.

Health ecosystem expansion: Android Health Connect integration and desktop website building support

In addition to the mobile interface changes, OpenAI is also broadening the scope of ChatGPT Health. The feature launched earlier this year and became available to all users in the United States in July; it previously supported integration with Apple Health.

Now, users can connect health and fitness data through Android Health Connect to gain insights into sleep, activity levels, and more. Dots can also use this health information to offer more proactive suggestions, such as recommending an alternative time when a calendar meeting conflicts with a workout session, or using connected medical records to remind users about preventive care services they may be eligible for.

In addition, users can build customized websites based on health data in the ChatGPT desktop app, such as creating a personal webpage to track workouts. OpenAI said these health-related updates will roll out to users gradually as planned.
